criteria.criterion: A unit test in steward.rs, using fresh job ids, shows queued_work returns unread Queued requests from both the steward and cli channels, oldest first (ties by job id), and excludes non-Queued jobs and other channels. Run `cargo test -p athena-core queued_work`.
criteria.evidence: Ran it: `steward::tests::unread_steward_and_cli_requests_are_queued_work_oldest_first ... ok`. I read the test. It uses ids none of the old ones match (2026101[2-6]-120000-*). Its records are two steward requests and two cli requests (the cli pair share a timestamp, so the tie is settled by job id), one closed cli job, and one 'web' job. It asserts the order [cccb, cccc, aaaa, bbbb], which shows both the exclusions and the ordering. Against the base filter (steward only) the test would fail.

criteria.criterion: A drain test with a cli-channel queued request (fresh id) shows drain lists and works it like a steward item. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli drain`.
criteria.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-cli drain` passed (8 unit tests and 4 tests in tests/drain.rs). That name filter does not select the new test, though, so I also ran it by name: `a_request_deferred_with_ask_later_is_listed_and_worked_like_a_steward_item ... ok`. The test queues a request through `athena.queue`, which records channel "cli" (reading.rs:521). It asserts the queue lists exactly that job, drain stops TargetMet, one job landed, the lander got that job, the outcome is 'passed', and the job left the queued state. Against the base code the queue would be empty and the test would fail.

findings.summary: The criterion's command `cargo test -p athena-cli drain` does not run the new cli-channel drain test.
findings.evidence: The name filter 'drain' does not match `a_request_deferred_with_ask_later_is_listed_and_worked_like_a_steward_item`. The new test only ran when I invoked it by name or ran the full suite. Both runs passed.

summary: The change does what was asked: `athena drain` now works requests queued with `athena ask --later`. The fix is in the one shared function that picks the drain's queue, `steward::queued_work`: it now keeps a request if its channel is in `DRAINED_CHANNELS`, which holds `steward` and `cli`. There is no special case for any job id. Ordering, the unread-only rule and retry are unchanged, and other channels are still left out. I confirmed in reading.rs that `ask --later` records the `cli` channel. A new unit test with fresh ids covers both channels, the oldest-first order with ties by job id, a closed job and a 'web' job. A new drain test shows a cli request is listed, worked, landed and rated. Both new tests would fail on the old code. Every doc that said the drain takes only the steward's channel is updated; D104 and a CHANGELOG line record the change and why. I ran the brief's commands in this snapshot and all passed: the queued_work test, the drain tests, the new drain test by name, the full test suite, clippy and fmt. Two minor findings: main.rs (the drain help text) changed although it is not on the deliverables list, and the criterion's `drain` test filter does not select the new test, which I ran separately.
